# Josh Lake, joshlake.ai

> Serial entrepreneur thinking about AI and the convergence of energy and intelligence. Colorado, USA.

## About Josh Lake

Josh Lake is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, and builder. He is currently focused on AI and the convergence of energy and intelligence — what becomes possible when both get cheap and abundant. He is the founder of Electrify Everything Now (free home electrification calculators). He co-founded Elephant Energy, a home electrification platform, and served as its CTO for five years. Earlier in his career, he was Head of Operations at Nuro (autonomous delivery), COO of Evercar/Vision Fleet (shared EV fleets), and Sr. Program Manager at Amonix (concentrated solar, world-record CPV modules). He holds a B.S. in Materials Science & Engineering from MIT and a Mechanical Engineering certificate from Stanford.

## Expertise

- AI and the convergence of energy and intelligence
- Speed to power: large load interconnection, queue reform, time-to-energized for data centers
- Grid capacity and risk: interconnection risk, curtailment risk, flexible load, behind-the-meter generation
- AI data center infrastructure and energy demand growth
- AI-native services businesses: delivering professional-services scope with agent-run workflows
- Agents for operations: multi-agent systems, agentic operating systems for companies
- Home electrification: heat pumps, induction stoves, EV chargers, electrical panels, smart load management
- AI implementation in small and mid-size companies
- Climate technology and clean energy
- Autonomous vehicles and electric vehicle operations
- Startup operations, scaling, and go-to-market

### The Path to 1 Trillion X Intelligence!
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/energy-to-abundance
- Description: Twelve learnings, observations, and quasi-predictions from building at the intersection of AI, energy, and the physical world, plus lots of podcasts, videos, and articles. Organized around a sequence: data centers use energy and GPUs to make tokens, models use tokens to make intelligence, humans and increasingly agents use that intelligence to invent primitives, those primitives become products that are perfected, scaled, and distributed, and those products create abundance (Energy → Tokens → Intelligence → Inventions → Products → Abundance). (1) Intelligence is the product of several multipliers, and a million, billion, or trillion X increase is inevitable: 1,000x, then 1,000,000x, eventually a quadrillion X, from stacking bigger models, model efficiency, falling token cost, parallel agents, better memory and context, better algorithms, bigger data centers, more data, and synthetic data, the same way Moore's Law produced an estimated 30 sextillion transistors since 1947. The marginal price of intelligence is heading to $0 while the gains compound and accelerate. We are at the beginning of a Cambrian explosion of ideas, products, and services. (2) Agents are the great catalyst, and there will be trillions of them accelerating innovation: loops, graphs, and a goal, the modular unit of the scientific process, across Claude Code, ChatGPT Codex, Grok Bot, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Muse, Instinct, and dots. Wiring agents together with LLMs, MCPs, and APIs is manufacturing and systems engineering, and automation is the on-ramp to invention. (3) We will invent 1,000x more amazing things and the impacts are unfathomable: first chat, then code, then reasoning models, now automation, agents, and loops, and next invention, which will be 1,000x automation and take 1,000x the compute. Most new invention will be combinatorial across drugs, materials, recipes, movies, and products. The wildcard is when the invention process itself gets automated and physical AI (robots) merges with digital AI in automated labs. References Mark Zuckerberg's essay "The Future Is For Everyone." Everyone can become a builder, and each invention accelerates the flywheel. (4) The core technologies are already good enough for a decade of inventions and products: the product overhang is enormous, with thousands of models across dozens of labs (Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, Qwen, xAI, Chinese models, open and closed) on Artificial Analysis, Hugging Face, and OpenRouter, and almost nothing built on top yet. As Nat Friedman argues, chat and coding tools and agents are barely the start. If every lab stopped training tomorrow there would still be a decade of products to build. (5) We will build 1,000x more software because it is simple and cheap: built with single prompts by one user, perfectly customized, run locally, never reviewed, and deleted or forgotten once it solves the problem. It may not even look like software, from Excel to world models that generate every game frame in real time, and it is hard to overstate the impact of everyone becoming a builder. (6) Business is evolving to value outcomes and impact over inputs and outputs. A useful ladder runs inputs (hours, employees, seats, tokens), outputs (reports, messages, actions, leads), outcomes (resolved problems, completed hires, saved energy, delivered capacity), and impacts (increased profit, avoided cost, better health, faster time-to-power). The farther down the ladder, the more valuable the offering and the harder measurement, attribution, and risk-sharing become, and for now humans still take responsibility for outputs and drive outcomes. AI helps define success up front and verify it was delivered. (7) We may all start vibe-living: like vibe coding with Claude Code or ChatGPT Codex, you request an outcome in plain English and name the spend, and software, robots, and capital assemble on the fly against a verifiable outcome, then come apart. Verification is the whole trick, personal agents are a huge step, and robotics is the next. Abundance abstracts away the effort and inputs it takes to get an outcome. (8) Routing of models, agents, tools, data centers, and robots will be huge, on capability, task complexity, cost, quality, reliability, data privacy, security, scalability, and repeatability. Tokens have different flavors and costs, workflows need different latencies and uptime, and training jobs are nothing like inference jobs. (9) Voice finally works and is worth trying again: fast and accurate across Wispr Flow, ChatGPT, and Tesla, everywhere except Siri. Most of the first draft was dictated, removing typing as a lifelong governor on thinking. (10) Speed to power, not chips, is the limiter today: the bottleneck has shifted from GPUs to watts (technically watt-hours), and lack of electricity at nearly any price is the biggest point of friction. Solar, wind, storage, geothermal, nuclear, and gas are all needed, and building more is how prices come down. The grid has more buffer than assumed: solar and batteries, flexible compute, virtual power plants, demand response, behind-the-meter gas, repurposed commercial and industrial sites with interconnection, modular data centers, and data centers overseas, in space, in homes (SPAN XFRA), and at commercial sites and corporate parks (Crusoe Spark). Energized megawatts are the binding constraint on the next decade. (11) There has never been a better time to start a company: cheap intelligence, an embarrassing product overhang, instantaneous free software, buyers who want outcomes, and routing that keeps the bill down. One person with a stack of agents covers what used to take a whole team. (12) There has never been a better time to be alive: an abundant future does not arrive on its own, it needs to get built, so have agency, get building, and have fun. The future is for everyone.

### A Neo-Electrification Company?
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/neo-electrification-company
- Description: Essay asking what a homeowner-centric, AI-enabled, national "neo-electrification" company would look like — one that combines heat pumps, solar and storage, electrical work, financing, incentives, field execution, and a home energy operating system. Maps the players circling the opportunity (heat pump installers like Elephant Energy, Jetson, Zero Homes, QuitCarbon, Quilt, and Forge; solar and storage platforms like Sunrun and Base Power; OEMs like Mitsubishi, Daikin, LG, and Carrier; utilities and CCAs; and smart-panel companies like SPAN). Argues AI's real value is reducing soft costs across design, incentives, marketing, commissioning, service, forecasting, working capital, and margin, and looks at European models (Aira, 1KOMMA5°, Thermondo, Enpal, Octopus). Concludes the winner will be semi-vertical, AI-enabled, nationally repeatable but locally excellent, utility-aware, and obsessed with project-level economics.

### Not All Tokens Are Equal
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/not-all-tokens-are-equal
- Description: Essay arguing that AI compute is not a single market. Maps the token economy into five workloads (capability creation, commodity batch, premium interactive, agentic outcome, local/autonomous), each with different economics, latency, geography, and power profile. Argues cheap energy and cheap intelligence are now the same race, and the next infrastructure winners will integrate compute, energy, networking, orchestration, capital, and physical deployment.

### This Is How I Would Implement AI at a 40-Person Startup
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/ai-at-a-startup
- Description: Practical playbook for implementing AI at a small (~40-person) company. Covers real leadership buy-in as prerequisite; the productivity-vs-transformation choice; standardizing on one LLM and one prototyping tool; distinguishing AI-empowered, AI-first, and AI-native; pragmatic guardrails and admitting policing is hard; solving for context before capability; crawl-walk-run maturity (agents, gems, and skills come last); treating agents like employees; restructuring roles, titles, and workflows; and building a shared culture of experimentation with leading indicators (adoption, happiness, token-maxing). Based on leading the AI rollout at Elephant Energy.

### The Electrification Sequencing Problem
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/electrification-sequencing
- Description: Decision framework for homeowners deciding what to electrify first. Covers appliance replacement timing, energy math by appliance type, panel capacity, solar sizing, and navigating the rebate landscape. Based on thousands of home electrification projects.

### You Probably Don't Need a Panel Upgrade
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/panel-upgrade-myth
- Description: Deep technical guide explaining why most homes do not need a $5,000-$10,000 electrical panel upgrade to electrify. Covers NEC Section 220.87 load studies, tandem breakers, load-sharing devices, dynamic load management, subpanels, and smart panels. Profiles 12 companies building panel-avoidance technology.
